title: Next steps in preparing for post-quantum cryptography
summary: NCSC whitepaper presenting post-quantum cryptography (PQC) as the best mitigation against the quantum threat to traditional public-key cryptography and setting out preparatory steps for organisations.

title: RFC 9794: a new standard for post-quantum terminology
summary: NCSC post introducing RFC 9794, a new standard for post-quantum cryptography terminology, in the context of NIST's publication of PQC standards.

title: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) pilot under the Assured Cyber Security Consultancy scheme
summary: NCSC pilot scheme assuring consultancies that meet the scheme Standard for post-quantum cryptography; assured consultancies will support the NCSC's PQC work with organisations.

title: Timelines for migration to post-quantum cryptography
summary: NCSC guidance setting dated milestones for PQC migration: discovery by 2028, highest-priority migration by 2031, and complete migration of all systems, services and products by 2035.

title: Migrating to post-quantum cryptography (NCSC Annual Review 2025 chapter)
summary: Chapter of the NCSC Annual Review 2025 describing migration to post-quantum cryptography as an international effort to protect against a future large-scale quantum computer.

title: Post-quantum cryptography (NCSC Annual Review 2024 chapter)
summary: Chapter of the NCSC Annual Review 2024 identifying migration to post-quantum cryptography as the primary mitigation against the quantum threat to current cryptography.

title: Perspectives on the plan for PQC transition
summary: Independent research published on GOV.UK setting out regulator and industry perspectives on the current plan for the transition to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Quantum computing, sensing and communications (POSTnote PN 0742)
summary: Research briefing by the Parliamentary Office of Science and Technology noting that the UK National Cyber Security Centre has recommended organisations start moving to post-quantum cryptographic methods now.

title: Quantum Technology - parliamentary written question and answer (40037)
summary: Parliamentary written question and government answer on quantum technology, referencing guidance focused on migrating to post-quantum cryptography to mitigate the future quantum threat to encryption services.

title: Quantum Technology - parliamentary written question and answer (8496)
summary: Parliamentary written question and government answer noting that, following publication of post-quantum cryptography standards, the NCSC has published details of how it will help organisations plan their migration to PQC.

title: Google Quantum Computing Chip - House of Commons debate (Hansard)
summary: Hansard record of a House of Commons debate on quantum computing in which post-quantum cryptography is discussed as the means to prevent the so-called Y2Q ('year to quantum') end of privacy.

title: The Bank of England's approach to innovation in artificial intelligence, DLT and quantum computing
summary: Bank of England report on its approach to technological innovation, including developed risk scenarios for post-quantum threats such as encrypted data harvesting and quantum-enhanced trading.

title: A systemic risk perspective on operational resilience (speech)
summary: Bank of England keynote speech stating that, given firm dependencies on third-party vendors, the transition to post-quantum cryptography is broader than individual firms' risk appetites.

title: 2025 CBEST thematic
summary: Bank of England thematic findings from CBEST threat-led penetration testing, noting that the work supports organisations' progress toward post-quantum cryptography (PQC) readiness, with discovery as a key milestone.

title: Financial Stability Report - December 2025
summary: Bank of England Financial Stability Report discussing post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and urging firms to prepare and plan for PQC migration now, including mapping the software and hardware needed.

title: Guidance for Post-Quantum Cryptography (April 2025)
summary: Guidance from the UK Cross Market Operational Resilience Group (CMORG) for the financial sector on managing quantum risk, aligned with the UK National Cyber Security Centre's PQC guidance. CMORG is a financial-sector resilience group rather than a government body, so flagged for review.

title: Written evidence to a UK Parliament committee on quantum technologies (121374)
summary: Written evidence submitted to a UK parliamentary committee discussing post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithms as classical algorithms hoped to be secure against quantum computers. Submitter could not be identified from the candidate, so flagged for review.

title: Written evidence on quantum technologies (QUT0015)
summary: Written evidence submitted to a UK parliamentary inquiry on quantum technologies, defining post-quantum cryptography as classical cryptographic protocols believed to be resilient to quantum computing attacks. Submitter could not be identified from the candidate, so flagged for review.

title: John Taylor questionnaire, January 2024
summary: Appointment questionnaire published by the Bank of England noting that quantum computing could undermine standard methods for encrypting data and referencing post-quantum cryptography. PQC mention is incidental to the document's purpose, so flagged for review.

title: Enhancing the Privacy of a Digital Pound (MIT report)
summary: Report on privacy-enhancing technologies for a digital pound, hosted by the Bank of England, stating that assessment of PETs for CBDCs should consider compatibility with post-quantum security. Authored by MIT researchers rather than the Bank itself, so flagged for review.

title: Quantum key distribution research report
summary: Independent research commissioned by the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT), published 10 June 2026, examining quantum key distribution (QKD) and its cyber security implications. It states that the UK NCSC advises post-quantum cryptography (PQC) as the preferred approach to the quantum threat and that QKD should be considered only as an additional layer alongside PQC, not a standalone solution.

title: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) migration workshop report
summary: NCSC report published 22 July 2026 on the UK's first PQC migration workshop, hosted with Vodafone in December 2025, concluding that no organisation can navigate the shift to post-quantum cryptography alone. It calls for board-level engagement, supply-chain collaboration and transparent cross-sector cooperation to meet the NCSC's migration milestones.

title: Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Bill - Lords Grand Committee debate, 1 September 2026
summary: Hansard record of the House of Lords Grand Committee sitting of 1 September 2026 on the Cyber Security and Resilience (NIS) Bill, in which Amendment 82 sought to place post-quantum cryptography and migration timelines into the statement of strategic priorities, with peers citing 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks. The responding Minister declined to mandate specific technologies, saying the department is developing guidance to support organisations' PQC transition in line with NCSC guidance.

title: The National Cyber Advisory Board
summary: GOV.UK page for the National Cyber Advisory Board, updated 31 July 2026, setting out the Board's workstreams. It states that on quantum the Board is 'organising an industry-government group to build engagement and momentum on post-quantum cryptography'.

title: Security Standard SS-007: Use of Cryptography (version 2.1)
summary: Department for Work and Pensions Chief Security Office cryptography standard (v2.1, approved 25 March 2025) that binds DWP suppliers and contractors, republished in the department's procurement security collection on 7 August 2026. Version 2.1 added quantum-resistant cryptography content, including a control section on quantum resistant algorithms and references to NIST post-quantum cryptography and NCSC PQC guidance.

title: Security Standard SS-002: Public Key Infrastructure & Key Management (version 2.1)
summary: Department for Work and Pensions Chief Security Office PKI and key management standard (v2.1, approved 25 March 2025) applying to DWP suppliers, republished in the procurement security collection on 7 August 2026. It states that quantum computing threatens public key infrastructure and that post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithms resistant to quantum attacks are being developed, pointing readers to NIST and NCSC PQC material.

title: Cyber Coordination Group insights 2025
summary: Financial Conduct Authority good and poor practice publication (24 April 2026) drawing on its Cyber Coordination Group of up to 140 UK financial services firms. It defines post-quantum cryptography and states that PQC migration must be embedded in existing risk frameworks with strong cryptographic hygiene and risk-based prioritisation, alongside role-specific PQC literacy programmes for staff.

title: Quantum Technology - parliamentary written question and answer (40038)
summary: Written question of 20 March 2025 to the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, answered 28 March 2025, on the guidance and resources available to help small and medium-sized enterprises prepare for and mitigate quantum cyber risks, with the answer referring to post-quantum cryptography migration.

title: Quantum Technology - parliamentary written question and answer (40039)
summary: Written question of 20 March 2025 to the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, answered 28 March 2025, asking for an assessment of the adequacy of the UK's contingency plans to tackle quantum cyber threats, with the answer referring to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Migrating to post-quantum cryptography (PQC)
summary: NCSC blog post (published 3 November 2023, updated 12 March 2025) introducing the NCSC's guidance on moving from traditional public-key cryptography to post-quantum cryptography. It notes that PQC can often be deployed by software update for major internet services but that legacy systems and critical infrastructure require phased planning and technology refresh.

title: Post-quantum cryptography: what comes next?
summary: NCSC blog post (14 August 2024, updated 13 March 2025) responding to NIST's publication of the ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA standards, stating that standardisation is only the start of migration to PQC. It sets out the NCSC's intention to accredit PQC consultancies and to publish further migration guidance, and is the reference cited in UK departmental cryptography standards.

title: Setting direction for the UK's migration to post-quantum cryptography
summary: NCSC blog post of 20 March 2025 accompanying the publication of the PQC migration timelines, explaining the three target dates of 2028 for discovery and planning, 2031 for priority migrations and 2035 for complete migration. It argues that the required activities align with fundamental cyber security practice such as asset management and supplier oversight, so the transition is relevant to organisations of all sizes.

title: Timeline for PQC migration revealed
summary: NCSC news announcement of 20 March 2025 unveiling the UK's three-phase roadmap for migration to quantum-resistant encryption by 2035. It summarises the phases as planning to 2028, high-priority upgrades from 2028 to 2031, and complete migration of all systems by 2035.

title: Preparing for post-quantum threat will make "fixing the Millennium Bug look easy"
summary: NCSC news item of 7 May 2025 reporting its Chief Technology Officer's warning that PQC migration is a decade-long, national-scale technology change more complex than the Millennium Bug remediation. It accompanies the launch of the NCSC's PQC consultancy scheme and migration guidance and urges vendors to build quantum-safe resilience into products.

title: G7 Cyber Expert Group 2026 Cross Border Coordination Exercise (CBCE)
summary: HM Treasury news item of 31 July 2026 reporting the conclusion of the G7 Cyber Expert Group's 2026 cross-border cyber crisis exercise, listing the transition to post-quantum cryptography among the group's recent focus areas and publications. Published by a UK department but reporting the work of an international body, and the PQC reference is incidental, so flagged for review.

title: Advancing a Coordinated Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography in the Financial Sector
issuingOrg: HM Treasury / G7 Cyber Expert Group
summary: Statement published on GOV.UK by HM Treasury on 13 January 2026 setting out the G7 Cyber Expert Group's high-level roadmap to help financial-sector organisations transition to post-quantum cryptography in a coordinated, timely and objective-driven way. Substantively a PQC document and a UK government publication, but authored by an international body, so flagged for review.

title: Preparing for Quantum-Safe Cryptography
summary: NCSC white paper (version 2.0, November 2020) explaining how quantum computing threatens public key cryptography and setting out quantum-safe cryptography as the mitigation, with advice on standardisation timing and organisational preparation. It cautions against early adoption of non-standardised quantum-safe algorithms.

title: 'Quantum-safe' cryptography (NCSC Annual Review 2021)
summary: Chapter of the NCSC Annual Review 2021 reporting that the NCSC designed its first quantum-safe cryptographic algorithms. It also states the NCSC plans to ready a quantum-safe version of its PRIME network protocol for vendor use.

title: Quantum security technologies
summary: NCSC white paper setting out its position on Quantum Key Distribution and Quantum Random Number Generation, replacing its earlier QKD white paper. It states that quantum-safe cryptography is the best mitigation against the quantum computing threat and advises that QKD users implement quantum-safe authentication alongside it.

title: Regulatory Priorities: Wholesale Markets, March 2026
summary: FCA Regulatory Priorities report for wholesale market firms (benchmark administrators, trading venues, wholesale banks and others), dated March 2026. Under its priority to enable the safe and responsible adoption of new technology, the FCA says it will continue to monitor sectoral progress with post-quantum cryptography and support insight sharing and knowledge dissemination.
